newsitem.title: CHINA: Repairs boost China's shipbuilding industry.
newsitem.headline: Repairs boost China's shipbuilding industry.

text.p: China's shipbuilding industry has significantly raised earnings from repairs but is also looking to boost its core industry, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
The China State Shipbuilding Corp earned 6.32 billion yuan ($759 million) in the first half of the year, up 20.5 percent year on year, the newspaper said.

Of this, 900 million yuan came from its ship repair business, an annual growth rate of 31.5 percent, it reported Zhou Guangqi, deputy director of the corporation's science and technology bureau, as saying.
The company received new orders for an aggregate 1.6 million deadweight tonnes in the period, the paper added.
Repairs of foreign ships had become a bulwark, with foreign currency earnings hitting $75.39 million, a 66.7 percent jump compared with the first half of last year, Zhou said.
The company can now build oil tankers and bulk carriers above 35,000 tonnes in 90 days compared with 120 days previously as a result of increased efficiency.

"Our advantage of using cheap labour as the only source for sustained growth has vanished gradually," Zhou said. "Instead we will continue to pursue intensive growth throught robust quality and advanced technology."
